item.description:
# Lab: Publish a SaaS

With **software as a service (SaaS)** products, you deploy and manage software in your AWS account and grant buyers access to the application. You are responsible for managing customer access, account creation, resource provisioning, and account management within your software.

In this lab, we create an initial product listing in AWS Marketplace in a limited state. Only your seller account and allowlisted test accounts can view and subscribe to this limited listing.

For complete workshop including intergrating with buyer onboarding, getting purchase updates and details, and reporting usage to charge the buyer, please refer to the [AWS Marketplace Workshop](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/use-cases/publish-saas).

item.description: ## **Background** AWS Marketplace Catalog API allows sellers to programmatically create and manage custom offers that only specific buyers can subscribe to (also known as _private offers_) instead of using the [AWS Marketplace Management Portal ](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/)  (seller portal). Sellers can also authorize specific resellers (also known as _channel partners_) to create private offers on their behalf (also known as _channel partner private offers_). ## **Lab overview** In this lab, you use an API to create a private offer for a SaaS product with the pricing model [Contract with Consumption](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/saas#pricing-models). - [Task 1: Create private offer](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/use-cases/create-saas-private-offer-with-api#task-1:-create-private-offer) - [Task 2: View private offer](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/use-cases/create-saas-private-offer-with-api#task-2:-view-private-offer) - [Task 3: Share private offer link](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/use-cases/create-saas-private-offer-with-api#task-3:-share-private-offer-link) ## **Prerequisites** - You must have an existing and public SaaS-based product in your seller AWS account with the pricing model [Contract with Consumption](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/saas#pricing-models) - **Public product required** The resulting SaaS product created in the [Lab: Publish a SaaS](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/use-cases/publish-saas) does not meet this prerequisite because that lab does not integrate with a real SaaS application and subsequently does not make the product public in AWS Marketplace. - You must have the following policy permissions in your AWS account IAM policies required [AWSMarketplaceSellerFullAccess: ](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/home#/policies/arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSMarketplaceSellerFullAccess$jsonEditor) _To submit offers for publishing._ ## Environment Make sure to configure environment variables under your **Lab Create SaaS Private Offer** Environment.

item.description: ## **Background** AWS Marketplace Catalog API allows sellers to programmatically create and manage custom offers that only specific buyers can subscribe to (also known as _private offers_ on AWS Marketplace) instead of using the [AWS Marketplace Management Portal ](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/)  (seller-facing portal on AWS Marketplace). Sellers can also authorize specific resellers (also known as _channel partners_) to create private offers on their behalf (also known as _channel partner private offers_). ## **Lab overview** In this lab, you use an API to authorize a reseller to create private offers on your behalf for a SaaS product with the pricing model [Contract with Consumption](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/saas#pricing-models). - [Task 1: Create resale authorization](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/use-cases/authorize-saas-reseller-with-api#task-1:-create-resale-authorization) - [Task 2: View resale authorization](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/use-cases/authorize-saas-reseller-with-api#task-2:-view-resale-authorization) ## **Prerequisites** - You must have an existing and public SaaS-based product in your seller AWS account with the pricing model [Contract with Consumption](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/saas#pricing-models) - **Public product required** The resulting SaaS product created in the [Lab: Publish a SaaS](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/use-cases/publish-saas) does not meet this prerequisite because that lab does not integrate with a real SaaS application and subsequently does not make the product public in AWS Marketplace. - You must have the following policy permissions in your AWS account IAM policies required [AWSMarketplaceSellerFullAccess: ](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/home#/policies/arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSMarketplaceSellerFullAccess$jsonEditor) _To submit offers for publishing._ [IAMFullAccess: ](https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/home#/policies/arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/IAMFullAccess$jsonEditor) _To create a service role that allows AWS Marketplace to share your product with resellers so that they can create offers on your behalf._ You also need to create a [service-linked role that allows AWS Marketplace to share your product with resellers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/using-roles-for-resale-authorization.html#slr-permissions)

## Submit Partner Originated Opportunity

Partners can manage opportunities created within their CRM systems and synchronize them with AWS Partner Central and associate AWS Marketplace Private Offer using the AWS Partner Central Selling API. We will work with Sandbox environment so your production instance will not be impacted. In this step, we will create an ACE opportunity, associate a solution with the opportunity and submit to AWS for review. After that, we will simulate the approval from AWS to approve the opportunity.

item.description:
# Lab: Multi-product solution - Solution set

AWS Marketplace Catalog API allows sellers to programmatically create and manage solution sets instead of using the [AWS Marketplace Management Portal ](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/)  (seller portal). A solution is a collection of products and services that work together to solve specific customer problems. Solutions can include AWS Marketplace products, non-AWS Marketplace products. Solutions must be paired with buyer engagement options to become discoverable and actionable for buyers on AWS Marketplace.

In this lab, you will explore API examples to create solution sets and provides examples of common operations for working with solutions using the AWS Marketplace Catalog API. The first two tasks will show you want you currently have and the 4 other labs will show how you can create, update, populate and publish your solution.

- [Task 1: List solutions](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-products-with-api/multi-product-solution-solution-set#task-1:-list-solutions)
    
- [Task 2: Get solution details](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-products-with-api/multi-product-solution-solution-set#task-2:-get-solution-details)
    
- [Task 3: Creating a solution](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-products-with-api/multi-product-solution-solution-set#task-3:-creating-a-solution)
    
- [Task 4: Updating solution information](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-products-with-api/multi-product-solution-solution-set#task-4:-updating-solution-information)
    
- [Task 5: Update related products](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-products-with-api/multi-product-solution-solution-set#task-5:-update-related-products)
    
- [Task 6: Release a solution](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-products-with-api/multi-product-solution-solution-set#task-6:-release-a-solution)
    

First workflow: List solutions -> Get solution details

Second workflow: Creating a solution → Updating solution information → Update related products → Release a solution

For more details, refer to the [official documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/work-with-solutions.html) and [workshop](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-products-with-api/multi-product-solution-solution-set).

# Lab: Multi-product solution - Offer set

AWS Marketplace Catalog API allows sellers to programmatically create and manage offer sets instead of using the [AWS Marketplace Management Portal ](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/)  (seller portal). The OfferSet entity helps sellers package multiple AWS Marketplace oﬀers into unified multi-product transactable packages. An OfferSet helps buyers discover and procure related products as a cohesive solution rather than individual components.

In this lab, you will explore API examples to create offer sets and provides examples of common operations for working with offers using the AWS Marketplace Catalog API. The 7 following tasks will show how you can create an offer set, add details, populate the offer set with individual offers, associate te offer set to a solution and publishing the offer set.

- [Task 1: Create offer set](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-offers-with-api/multi-product-solution-offer-set#task-1:-create-offer-set)
    
- [Task 2: Update information](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-offers-with-api/multi-product-solution-offer-set#task-2:-update-information)
    
- [Task 3: Associate offers](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-offers-with-api/multi-product-solution-offer-set#task-3:-associate-offers)
    
- [Task 4: Disassociate offers](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-offers-with-api/multi-product-solution-offer-set#task-4:-disassociate-offers)
    
- [Task 5: Associate solution](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-offers-with-api/multi-product-solution-offer-set#task-5:-associate-solution)
    
- [Task 6: Disassociate solution](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-offers-with-api/multi-product-solution-offer-set#task-6:-disassociate-solution)
    
- [Task 7: Release offer set](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-offers-with-api/multi-product-solution-offer-set#task-7:-release-offer-set)
    

Create offer set → Update information → Associate offers → Associate solution → Release offer set

For more details, refer to the [official documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/work-with-offer-sets.html) and [workshop](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-offers-with-api/multi-product-solution-offer-set).

item.description: ### Purpose This folder walks through setting up **Amazon EventBridge rules and CloudWatch log targets** to capture AWS Marketplace events — specifically for monitoring when channel partner private offers (CPPOs) are created and when buyers accept them. --- ### Structure The folder is split into two parallel tracks — [ISV](https://desktop.postman.com/?desktopVersion=11.85.1&webVersion=11.85.1-ui-260219-0947&userId=38157848&teamId=6434732®ion=us#) and [Channel Partner](https://desktop.postman.com/?desktopVersion=11.85.1&webVersion=11.85.1-ui-260219-0947&userId=38157848&teamId=6434732®ion=us#) — each with the same two sub-folders but using different AWS credentials (vault-stored ISV vs. CP keys). #### **Setup** (8 requests each) Runs through the full infrastructure setup in order: 1. **CreateLogGroup** — Creates a CloudWatch log group to receive events. 2. **SetRetentionPolicy** _(optional)_ — Sets a 7-day log retention policy. 3. **VerifyLogGroup** — Confirms the log group exists and saves its ARN as `log_group_arn`. 4. **CreateEventBridgeRule** — Creates an EventBridge rule that listens for two Marketplace events: `Offer Released` (from `aws.marketplacecatalog`) and `Purchase Agreement Created` (from `aws.agreement-marketplace`). Saves the rule ARN as `eventbridge_rule_arn`. 5. **PutTargets-CloudWatch** — Wires the EventBridge rule to the CloudWatch log group as its target. 6. **PutResourcePolicyForCloudWatchLog** — Grants EventBridge permission to write to the log group. 7. **VerifyEventBridgeRule** — Confirms the rule was created correctly. 8. **VerifyEventBridgeTarget** — Confirms the CloudWatch target is attached. #### **CheckEvents** (2 requests each) Used after the setup to query the logs and verify events were captured: - **CheckForCreatedCPPOFromLogGroup** — Searches logs for a specific `OFFER_ID`, confirming a Channel Partner Private Offer (CPPO) was created. - **CheckForAcceptedOfferFromLogGroup** — Searches logs for a `Purchase Agreement Created` event, confirming a buyer accepted the offer. Both requests auto-calculate a 24-hour time window via pre-request scripts. --- ### In Summary This folder automates the end-to-end setup of an **event monitoring pipeline** for AWS Marketplace, enabling both ISVs and Channel Partners to independently verify that their private offer workflows are triggering the expected events — all captured in CloudWatch via EventBridge.

item.description: ### Purpose This folder contains requests for an **ISV (Independent Software Vendor)** to create and manage **Resale Authorizations** on AWS Marketplace using the Catalog API. A Resale Authorization allows an ISV to grant a Channel Partner the rights to resell their product. --- ### Requests 1. [ISV_CreateResaleAuthorization](https://desktop.postman.com/?desktopVersion=11.85.1&webVersion=11.85.1-ui-260219-0947&userId=38157848&teamId=6434732®ion=us#) — `POST {{_.CAPI_PROD}}/StartChangeSet` Initiates a new Resale Authorization by submitting a `ChangeSet` to the Marketplace Catalog API. This is the primary step where the ISV defines the terms of the resale agreement. 2. [ISV_CheckResaleAuthStatus](https://desktop.postman.com/?desktopVersion=11.85.1&webVersion=11.85.1-ui-260219-0947&userId=38157848&teamId=6434732®ion=us#) — `GET {{_.CAPI_PROD}}/DescribeChangeSet` Polls the status of the `ChangeSet` submitted in the previous step using `{{changeSetId}}`, allowing you to confirm whether the authorization was successfully created. 3. item.description:
This folder represents the **channel partner's perspective** in the CPPO (Channel Partner Private Offer) workflow on AWS Marketplace. It uses channel partner-specific AWS credentials and covers two CPPO creation scenarios along with the supporting requests to monitor and inspect the results.

## Workflow

```
1. Create a CPPO (or Replacement Offer)
        ↓
2. Poll for changeset completion (CP_CheckCPPOStatus)
        ↓
3. Inspect the resulting offer entity (CP_DescribeCPPO)
```

## Request Breakdown

**CP_CreateCPPO** — `POST /StartChangeSet`
Creates a new CPPO from a resale authorization granted by an ISV. It atomically creates the offer using `{{RESALE_AUTHORIZATION_ID}}`, applies a **5% markup**, targets a specific buyer (`{{BUYER_ID}}`), sets a validity term, attaches Standard EULA legal terms, and releases the offer immediately. A pre-request script auto-calculates the availability date (7 days from today), and the post-response script saves the returned `ChangeSetId` into `{{changeSetId}}` for downstream use.

**CP_CheckCPPOStatus** — `GET /DescribeChangeSet`
Polls the status of the submitted changeset using `{{changeSetId}}`. The post-response script implements an automated **retry loop**: on `SUCCEEDED` it extracts and saves `OFFER_ID`; on `FAILED` it halts execution; otherwise it waits ~4 seconds and re-polls. This enables non-blocking, fully automated polling in a collection run.

**CP_DescribeCPPO** — `GET /DescribeEntity`
Retrieves the full metadata and content of the created CPPO using `{{OFFER_ID}}`. Returns pricing terms, legal terms, buyer targeting rules, offer state, and the originating `ResaleAuthorizationId` — used to verify and inspect the published offer.

**CP_CreateReplacementOfferUsingResaleAuthorization** — `POST /StartChangeSet`
Creates a **replacement CPPO** for a buyer with an existing agreement (`{{AGREEMENT_ID}}`), used in amendment/renewal (ABO) scenarios. It ties the new offer to both the resale authorization and the existing agreement, auto-calculates a new availability date (1 day from today) and validity term (12 months from agreement expiry), and releases immediately.

## Summary

The Channel Partner folder provides a complete, automated toolkit for a channel partner to **create, monitor, and inspect private offers** on AWS Marketplace via the Catalog API. It handles both new CPPO creation and replacement offers for existing agreements, with built-in scripting for dynamic date calculation, automated changeset polling, and variable chaining — making it suitable for both manual and fully automated collection runs.
